newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-DE BILDE FACES COURT ACTION AFTER PUNCHING PLAYER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DE BILDE FACES COURT ACTION AFTER PUNCHING PLAYER.

text.p: Belgian club Aalst on Sunday urged Krist Porte to sue Belgium striker Gilles De Bilde for punching Porte in the face during a league match on Saturday, breaking his nose and eye socket.
"I had several examinations this morning. My nose and eye socket are both fractured in several places," Porte told BRTN radio from his hospital bed.

A television report said Porte also suffered slight concussion and possibly a torn retina in the incident which occurred when he tried to prevent De Bilde from rushing towards goal as Anderlecht's Par Zetterberg took a penalty.

Former Aalst player De Bilde, who has often performed below par this season and endured a barrage of criticism in recent weeks, wrestled himself free from Porte and appeared to hit him with his left fist.
De Bilde, who was not sent off and completed the match, had to stand trial last year for assault after head-butting a male nurse and punching another.

Porte, who left the pitch with a blood-covered face and was taken to hospital, said he had not decided yet whether to take legal action against De Bilde, who was suspended until further notice by Anderlecht.
"We have to show to everyone that we do not accept this," Anderlecht coach Johan Boskamp said.

"Porte has to respect himself and, of course, do a number of things to protect himself. Just imagine that there is permanent injury," Aalst manager Patrick Orlans said. "He might be unable to work for several months," he added.
De Bilde, who won the 1994 award for best Belgian league player, attacked the nurses when he was denied access to a hospital room where his father was being treated for a heart attack in August 1995.
BRTN said that Aalst themselves would not sue De Bilde but challenge the outcome of the game which they lost 3-0.

"First I thought the Aalst player had pulled or pushed a bit and our man had reacted...but later I saw clearly that Gilles made a gesture that was unacceptable," Anderlecht manager Michel Verschueren told BRTN radio.
"We see ourselves a bit as his father -- he did something wrong for which he has to be sanctioned but I hope...that they don't break him," he said.

"I think that on a psychological level that boy is entitled to assistance. I think that perhaps he should have an open discussion with a specialist in psycholigacal affairs, perhaps more than one to try and find his balance again," he said.
